title: S3 Bucket Policy Changes

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.7 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.7 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (eventName="PutBucketPolicy" OR eventName="PutBucketAcl" OR eventName="PutBucketPublicAccessBlock" OR eventName="DeleteBucketPolicy")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.7_s3_bucket_policy_changes_7"
| sort -_time
description: S3 bucket policy changes can expose sensitive data to the public internet. One of the most common cloud security incidents.
value: Detecting s3 bucket policy changes early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Critical alert on any bucket policy change. Extra-critical when `PutBucketPublicAccessBlock` is disabled or when ACLs grant public access. Integrate with AWS Config for continuous compliance.
visualization: Events list (critical), Table, Single value (policy changes last 7d).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where All_Changes.object_category="bucket" OR match(All_Changes.object, "(?i)s3:|arn:aws:s3:::")
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object All_Changes.action span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Change (All_Changes): for CloudTrail management events mapped to CIM. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Planned public static sites, migration cutovers, or content changes where security still reviewed the bucket policy.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Critical alert on any bucket policy change. Extra-critical when `PutBucketPublicAccessBlock` is disabled or when ACLs grant public access. Integrate with AWS Config for continuous compliance.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (eventName="PutBucketPolicy" OR eventName="PutBucketAcl" OR eventName="PutBucketPublicAccessBlock" OR eventName="DeleteBucketPolicy")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.7_s3_bucket_policy_changes_7"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect s3 bucket policy changes. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_7_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Events list (critical), Table, Single value (policy changes last 7d)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of s3 bucket policy changes so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
